title: C2385C — Audio digital signal processing (DSP) module connector
introduction:
I use this reference as the DSP connector’s seating chart: the drawing locates each cavity, and the assignment table explains which signal belongs there. Start with the connector identity and harness heading, find a cavity label in the drawing, then read across its matching table row.

The Function column separates audio enable, speaker connections, ground and the fuse-or-circuit-breaker connection. Read the speaker location and polarity together; a wire’s color alone does not explain its job. Grey-filled positions in the drawing correspond to table rows without assigned circuits or functions.

This page supports identification and table reading. It supplies no physical access, disconnection, probing, electrical test or splice procedure. Physical viewing direction, gauge convention and the meanings of Size and Used codes are not defined here. Keep those entries as printed; the service-parts table identifies catalog entries without establishing a replacement or wiring method.

edits.why: I use the outline as a landmark before matching cavity labels to table rows. As printed, the housing projection is on the left, with a long cavity column beside a shorter column on the right. These are drawing landmarks, not instructions for releasing the connector.

Cavity identifies a position in the drawing; Circuit Number identifies the circuit assigned to that position. Read across the same row for Color, Gauge, Function, Qualifier and Terminal Part Number. The speaker location and polarity distinguish the channel connections, while the ground row describes a separate function. Blank circuit and function cells do not supply an additional connection to interpret.

The Service Part and Engineering Shell columns identify different catalog fields. I keep them separate from the Terminal Part Number entries in the assignment table. The pigtail Gauge entry remains literal; this reference does not define it as a range or explain how to adapt its leads to the installed wiring.
